h: Steel City Extras to Pair With Your Round
p: Sheffield's city centre has a few gems that sit perfectly alongside a quick game of crazy golf. The Winter Garden is a huge city-centre glasshouse filled with plants from around the world, and it's free to wander through. Right next door, the Millennium Gallery showcases art, design and the city's famous metalwork, so you can see how Sheffield earned its name as the Steel City.

Fancy something a bit more hands-on? Kelham Island Museum, on the edge of the centre, tells the story of the city's industrial past with huge machines, including a mighty steam engine. The Kelham Island area around it has become a lively spot for food and drink too.

For the golf itself, here are a few tactics to try. Take a look at each hole before you start and think about angles; bouncing off the side walls is often quicker than going straight. A smooth, gentle putt usually works better than a big hit. And keep a sense of humour, because the ball will almost certainly do something ridiculous at least once.

If you've got younger kids with you, set a maximum number of shots per hole so nobody gets stuck. A bit of encouragement and the odd "that one doesn't count" goes a long way. Most groups find that the scorecard matters a lot less than the laughs by the end.
